text: Morris suddenly threw the paw. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> But Mister White cried out. <break time="0.8s" /> And quickly pulled it out again. <break time="0.8s" /> If you were wise. <break time="0.8s" /> You would let it burn. <break time="0.8s" /> The soldier said. <break time="0.8s" /> But Mister White wanted to keep it. <break time="0.8s" /> Before he left. <break time="0.8s" /> Morris warned his friend once more. <break time="0.8s" /> If you must wish. <break time="0.8s" /> Wish for something sensible. <break time="0.8s" /> After Morris had gone. <break time="0.8s" /> Herbert laughed and said that the story of the paw. <break time="0.8s" /> Was probably just another soldiers tale. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister White held the paw and said that he did not know what to wish for because he already had everything. <break time="0.8s" /> If you only cleared. <break time="0.8s" /> The debt on the house. <break time="0.8s" /> You would be quite happy. <break time="0.8s" /> Herbert said. <break time="0.8s" /> So wish for two hundred pounds. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding the paw up high. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister White said the words clearly. <break time="0.8s" /> I wish for two hundred pounds. <break time="0.8s" /> At that moment. <break time="0.8s" /> He gave a cry and dropped the paw. <break time="0.8s" /> Saying that it had twisted. <break time="0.8s" /> In his hand like a snake. <break time="0.8s" /> But no money appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> And the three sat by the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> In a silence. <break time="0.8s" /> That felt strangely heavy. <break time="0.8s" /> Before going to bed. <break time="0.8s" /> Herbert joked that they would find the money. <break time="0.8s" /> In a big bag. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of their bed.
